## Upstream changes 6.69.1 -> 6.70.0

**Verdict:** NEEDS ATTENTION — a breaking import-format change affects `aws_route53domains_delegation_signer_record`, and the version pin in `01-providers.tf` must be widened before `terraform init` will even pick up 6.70.0.

### Breaking changes
- `resource/aws_route53domains_delegation_signer_record: Change the format of the import ID from domain_name,dnssec_key_id to domain_name,flags,algorithm,public_key. This is acceptable in a minor version because AWS no longer return DNSKEY flags and delegation signer records can no longer reliably be found by domain name and key ID` (#50522). Only relevant if this template, or a stack built from it, manages or has imported an `aws_route53domains_delegation_signer_record` resource. Any existing import ID in scripts, state-import tooling, or documentation using the old `domain_name,dnssec_key_id` format will no longer work.

### Variables
- none — this is a Terraform provider, not a templated application; there is no `.env.example` entry for it. The relevant pin is in `01-providers.tf`:
  `version = "~> 6.69.1"` — this constraint caps the provider at `6.69.x` and must be changed (e.g. to `~> 6.70.0` or a wider range) for the upgrade to take effect at all.

### Data and dependencies
- none found in the notes beyond the above. No companion service (database, cache, search engine) version requirement is named by this release.

### Before applying
- Edit `01-providers.tf` and raise the `aws` provider version constraint from `~> 6.69.1` to permit 6.70.0 (e.g. `~> 6.70.0`), then run `terraform init -upgrade`.
- Search the codebase/state for any use of `aws_route53domains_delegation_signer_record` import commands or automation; if present, update them to the new `domain_name,flags,algorithm,public_key` import ID format before relying on re-imports.
- Run `terraform plan` after upgrading and inspect it for unexpected diffs on any `aws_route53domains_delegation_signer_record`, `aws_guardduty_detector_feature`, `aws_guardduty_member_detector_feature`, or `aws_guardduty_organization_configuration_feature` resources — several bug fixes in this release change how `additional_configuration`/`RDS_DATA_RISK` defaults are read and may produce a one-time diff.
- No state backup is strictly required by anything in the notes, but a `terraform state pull` backup before any provider upgrade is good practice given this template's state is S3/DynamoDB-backed.

### Notes read
- `v6.70.0` (2026-10-21) and `v6.69.1` (2026-10-15, baseline) from the hashicorp/terraform-provider-aws CHANGELOG, as pasted above. The registry image-diff section could not be read (401 Unauthorized), so container-level claims (user, entrypoint, ports, etc.) are not applicable here — this is a Terraform provider binary, not a long-running service image — and are not part of this verdict.

## Upstream changes 0.21.0 -> 0.21.1

**Verdict:** NEEDS ATTENTION — the agent emits a changed stats payload (deprecated legacy memory/swap fields alongside new byte fields), and the hub side of this template is still pinned to 0.21.0, which does not populate the new fields; no action is strictly required but the pairing is worth checking.

### Breaking changes
- Agent stats payload shape changes. Per the notes: "existing memory fields other than memory percentage are deprecated in favor of new fields which provide raw byte values. The deprecated fields are still populated, but will be removed from the API in a future version." This affects `henrygd/beszel-agent`, the image this review is scoped to. The new byte fields are "populated on hub version 0.21.1+ for all agents" — since this template's hub (`henrygd/beszel`) stays pinned to 0.21.0 unless separately upgraded, the new fields will simply not appear yet; nothing breaks, but the agent is not giving the hub its full new data until the hub is also moved to 0.21.1.
- For Go-package consumers, `Agent.Start` now requires a `context.Context`. Not applicable to this template — it runs the prebuilt image, not the Go package.
- No other breaking change in the agent's runtime behaviour is named in the notes for this range.

### Variables
- None. No renamed, removed or newly required environment variables are mentioned for the agent in these notes. `HUB_HEADERS` is a new optional variable ("Add `HUB_HEADERS` environment variable to set custom WebSocket headers on the agent (#2585)") — not required, not in `.env.example`, nothing to act on.
- `CONTAINER_NAME_LABEL` is listed as new but is a hub-side convenience, not consumed by the agent service in this compose file.

### Data and dependencies
- None introduced by this range. The template's existing agent/hub pairing requirement, its socket-based hub/agent channel, and the `-alpine` variant requirement for S.M.A.R.T. are all already true at 0.21.0 and are not changes in this upgrade.
- WHAT THE IMAGES THEMSELVES DIFFER IN confirms user, entrypoint, cmd, ports, volumes, healthcheck and environment are all identical between 0.21.0 and 0.21.1 for `henrygd/beszel-agent` — nothing in the container's run contract moved. The verdict here rests entirely on the described change to the stats payload format, which is inside the application rather than the image configuration, and the notes remain authoritative for that.

### Before applying
- No backup or manual migration step is required for the agent alone.
- If full benefit of this release is wanted (raw byte memory/swap fields reaching the hub UI/API), plan to upgrade `BESZEL_IMAGE_VERSION` (hub) to 0.21.1 as well, in the same change window. Until then the agent will keep sending the deprecated GB fields that the 0.21.0 hub expects, which is the supported fallback path per the notes ("still populated ... for older hubs").
- No `.env` or compose edits are needed for this agent bump specifically.

### Notes read
- v0.21.1 (2026-10-22) — upgrade target, read in full.
- v0.21.0 (2026-10-02) — given as the current-baseline release, read only to exclude already-true requirements from this verdict.
- No UPGRADING, BREAKING_CHANGES or CHANGELOG document was supplied beyond the release notes above; none was available to cross-check.
